html:
SMTO-RST-0023 — An older SMTO version turned this work away to save memory

GUID: f6266cc2-251f-57b4-a4c7-1fefff37d53c
Slug: controller-memory-pressure
Domain: RST · Subsystem: controller

What happened

  • An earlier version of SMTO refused new work when it thought memory was running low. Current SMTO no longer has that limit, so this message only records something that happened before.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation and look for the task you sent around the time of this message, including in the Prompt queue. This old refusal says nothing about later attempts, so the work may already have run.
  2. If the task isn't there and never ran, send it again. Current SMTO doesn't refuse work for this memory reason any more.
  3. If you see this message for brand-new work today, ask the person who manages SMTO to update it to the current version. Only older versions of SMTO give this refusal, so seeing it now means an old server is still running.

What success looks like

  • Your task appears in the conversation and starts running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the time you sent the task, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send the same task several times; check first so it doesn't run twice. There's no memory setting to change.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An older Controller rejected a submission through its retired memory-budget admission gate (logical state plus cached RSS above a fixed budget minus reserve); current Controllers have no such gate and ignore the old options.

What this means

  • Earlier controllers compared logical state size and cached RSS with a fixed memory budget minus reserve and could reject submissions with HTTP 503. Current controllers impose no application memory budget and ignore the old options. Memory usage is diagnostic only; the operating system handles allocation and exhaustion. Historical records remain unchanged.

Why this can happen

  • The recorded controller used the retired application memory-budget policy.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the saved error with the running controller version; current memory diagnostics do not gate submissions.

How to fix it

  • Compare the error's recorded time with the running controller version; current controllers impose no application memory budget and ignore the old options, and there is no memory-budget setting to adjust. If new submissions still return this error, the process is an outdated build: restart on the updated controller after current work settles, and check task history before resubmitting.
  • Check the recorded occurrence time and running controller version. If new work produces this error, restart with the updated controller after current work settles. There is no memory-budget setting to adjust.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm whether the intended task was accepted before submitting it again. The updated controller has no memory-cap admission requirement.

How to verify the fix

  • The updated controller accepts new work without an application memory cap.

What not to do

  • Do not delete task history or blindly duplicate an accepted task.

Technical notes

  • The error identity is retained for history and is no longer emitted by current configuration validation or task submission.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
